stem: A 12-year-old boy with a painful deformed leg from a quadbike rollover receives IV morphine after cannulation. Which adverse effect of IV morphine is most important to monitor immediately in the trauma setting?
explanation: In acute trauma care, the most important immediate adverse effect of IV morphine is respiratory depression, because it can compromise airway and ventilation. Other opioid adverse effects may occur, but they are less immediately dangerous.

citations.title: Practice Quiz: Emergency Medicine - Trauma 2 - Pain

rationale: Although multiple opioid adverse effects are clinically relevant, the single best answer in the acute trauma setting is respiratory depression because it is the most dangerous immediate complication.

optionExplanations.A: Constipation is a common opioid adverse effect, but it is not an immediate trauma concern after a single IV dose.
optionExplanations.B: Dependence is associated with longer-term opioid use, not the immediate post-dose trauma setting.
optionExplanations.C: Correct: respiratory depression is the key acute adverse effect to monitor after IV morphine in trauma.
optionExplanations.D: Itching can occur due to histamine release, but it is usually less clinically urgent than respiratory depression.
optionExplanations.E: Nausea and vomiting are common, but they are not the most important immediate adverse effect in trauma.

source.questionTextHtml:
Following insertion of an IV cannula, Brayden receives a dose of IV morphine with good response on his pain score.

Which of the following adverse effects of IV morphine needs to be taken into account in trauma? Please note more than one answer may be correct.

Clinical scenario 1 - Braydon

The following six questions refer to Brayden’s clinical scenario.

Teaching/learning points:

Pain relief

Primary survey in context of distracting injury

Paramedics arrive in the emergency department with Brayden, a 12 year old boy. They were called to attend after Brayden lost control of his quadbike (recreational vehicles) while riding around in a field. He was found on his back, alert and screaming in pain. Eyewitnesses stated he had been travelling at approximately 40kph when he lost control at a bend and the quadbike rolled.

Brayden has an obvious deformity to his right lower limb. He was wearing a helmet, which was removed at the scene. He is transported to ED on a spinal board with hard collar in situ. Vital signs are Resp rate 28/min, Sats 100% in air, Heart rate 100bpm, BP 118/65. He has a grossly deformed right leg, with a firm, swollen thigh and he is screaming in pain.
